*****NOTE FROM THE CITY: PUBLIC PARTICIPATION: Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency and the social
distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20 (https://www.gov.ca.gov/wp-
content/uploads/2020/03/3.17.20-N-29-20-EO.pdf).

Please note that members of the public will be allowed to observe and/or address the City Council Meeting
  of March 9, 2021, at 2:00 P.M. for open session as follows:

  1.  Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit comments electronically for
  consideration by the Inglewood City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking
  Authority/Joint Powers Authority (Legislative Body) by sending them to the City Clerk/Secretary at
  athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the
  members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit comments prior to 8:00 A.M. the
  day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda number or subject matter.
  Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after 8:00 A.M. and prior to
  the close of the public hearings, will be made part of the official public record of the meeting. Contact the Office of the
  City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

  2.  By Telephone -Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public Comments: Members of the public can
  participate in the meeting by telephone to listen and make comments noting the following:

  l  The conference begins at 1:30 p.m., Pacific Time, and all interested parties may join the conference 5 minutes prior.
  l  If you are dialing in from a cell phone, please call from an area with good reception. Calls from landline phones are
  highly recommended.
  l If you are watching the meeting via Social Media or Channel 35 while also accessing the phone line, it is requested
  that you mute the sound of your video feed as it is delayed from the phone transmission. Additionally, when you are
  making public comments on the phone line, you will be inaudible due to feedback.
  l Dial-In: 1-888-251-2949 or 1-215-861-0694 using the specific access codes detailed below for the respective City
  Council Dates:

  ¡ March 16, 2021 – Access Code: 5914683#
  ¡ March 23, 2021 – Access Code: 5914683#
  ¡ March 30, 2021 – Access Code: 5914683#

  3.  Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:
   ¡ March 9, 2021 – Access Code: 5914683#
  ¡ March 16, 2021 – Access Code: 5914683#
  ¡ March 23, 2021 – Access Code: 5914683#
  ¡ March 30, 2021 – Access Code: 5914683#

  3.  Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:

  l  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider for details.

The above access options provide the public with the opportunity to both observe and listen to the meeting; however,
members of the public who wish to orally address the Legislative Body must use the public access options 1 and 2 noted
above.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
alternative formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of the Americans with
Disabilities Act of 1990 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and regulations adopted in
implementation thereof. Any person who requires a disability-related modification or accommodation, or

modification, accommodation, or service by contacting the Office of the City Clerk by telephone at 310-
412-5280, FAX at 310-412-5533, One Manchester Boulevard, First Floor, Inglewood City Hall,
Inglewood, CA 90301 or via email to athompson@cityofinglewood.org and aallen@cityofinglewood.org
no later than 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting.

Inglewood, California
  March 9, 2021

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  March 9, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  MAYOR/CHAIRMAN PRO TEM APPOINTMENT. It was moved by Council
  Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla, and seconded
  by Council Member/Successor Agency/Housing Authority Member Faulk that the City
  Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority does hereby appoint Council Member
  Morales a Mayor/Chairman Pro Tem for City Council Meeting. The motion was carried
  by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Faulk;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Mayor Butts.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Pro Tem/Chairman
  Pro Tem Morales called the City Council, Successor Agency, and Housing Authority into
  joint session at the hour of 2:02 p.m.

  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
  presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor Pro Tem /Successor Agency Pro Tem
  Chairman/Housing Authority Pro Tem Chairman
  Morales,  Council Members/Successor  Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Dotson, Padilla,
  and Faulk; and
  Absent:  Mayor Butts.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
  follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor Pro Tem/Successor Agency Pro
  Tem Chairman/Housing Authority Pro Tem Chairman Morales inquired if there were any
  persons present who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing
  Authority on any item on the Agendas other than the public hearing.
  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on Warrants and Bills, and Agenda Item Nos. 2, 3,
  PH-1.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Dotson, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  March 4, 2021, in the amount of $3,551,276.55 are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Pro Tem/Successor Agency Pro Tem
  Chairman/Housing Authority Pro Tem Chairman Morales;
  Noes: None; and

  1
   Absent: Mayor Butts.

301  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – ORDINANCE NO. 21-05 INTRODUCED –
  GRANTING STATE WATER COMPANY FRANCHISE.  The City Clerk
  announced the next scheduled matter was a public hearing to consider an ordinance
  granting Golden State Water Company a franchise to use or lay and use pipelines and
  appurtenances for transmitting and distributing water under, along, across or upon the
  public streets, ways, alleys and places within the City of Inglewood, and that the notice
  was given in the time, form and manner as required by law, an affidavit was on file, and
  no communication were received.

  Louis Atwell, Assistant City Manager/ Public Works Director, presented the staff report
  dated March 9, 2021.

  Mayor Pro Tem Morales ordered the staff report received and filed.

  Mayor Pro Tem Morales inquired if there were any persons present that wished to
  address the City Council on the matter.

  Caller (Name Unknown) thanked the City Council for clarity in regards to Ordinance No.
  21-05. She also requested that her phone calls are returned.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Council Member Padilla, and seconded by
  Council Member Dotson that further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Pro Tem Morales; and
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Mayor Butts

  Thereupon, Ordinance No. 21-05 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA GRANTING TO GOLDEN STATE
  WATER COMPANY, A CALIFORNIA CORPORATION, A
  FRANCHISE TO USE OR LAY AND USE PIPELINES AND
  APPURTENANCES FOR TRANSMITTING AND DISTRIBUTING
  WATER UNDER, ALONG, ACROSS, OR UPON THE PUBLIC
  STREETS, WAYS, ALLEYS, AND PLACES WITHIN THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD

  was introduced by Mayor Pro Tem Morales. The motion was carried by the following roll
  call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Pro Tem Morales;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Mayor Butts.

126  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council
  Member Morales that the Minutes for the City Council Meetings held on July 7, 2020,
  and July 14, 2020, be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Pro Tem Morales;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Mayor Butts.

131.8  RESOLUTION NO. 21-75 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE BUDGET FOR
  FISCAL YEAR 2020-2021 TO CARRY OVER UNSPENT COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT CARES ACT FUNDING. Staff report dated
  March 9, 2021, was presented recommending adoption of a resolution amending Fiscal
  Year 2020-2021 Budget to carry over unspent Community Development Block Grant
  CARES Act Funding (CDBG-CV) in the amount of $1,000,000 that was earmarked for
  the COVID-19 Rent Relief Program in Fiscal Year 2019-2020.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Morales that

  2
   the City Council does hereby adopt Resolution No. 21-75 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2020-2021 BUDGET FOR
  THE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT CARES ACT
  FUNDING FOR THE COVID-19 RENT RELIEF PROGRAM IN THE
  AMOUNT OF 1,000,000
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Pro Tem Morales;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Mayor Butts

. 172  RESOLUTION NO. 21-76 ADOPTED – MODIFYING THE TERMS AND
  CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT OF EMPLOYEES REPRESENTED BY
  IMEO/AFSCME LOCAL 960. Staff report dated March 9, 2021, was presented
  recommending adoption of a resolution effecting modification to the terms and
  conditions of employment of employees represented by IMEO/AFSCME Local 960.

  It was moved by Council Member Padilla, and seconded by Council Member Dotson that
  the City Council does hereby adopt Resolution No. 20-133 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA  APPROVING  AND  EFFECTUATING  THE
  UNDERSTANDING REACHED WITH THE INGLEWOOD MANAGEMENT
  EMPLOYEE ORGANIZATION (IMEO)/AFSCME LOCAL 960, PURSUANT
  TO THE STATE MEET AND CONFER LAWS

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Pro Tem Morales;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Mayor Butts

132.6  REPORTS–CITY CLERK. The City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson, paid tribute to
  Delores Huerta in honor of National Women’s History Month, closing with one of her
  quotes.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Pro Tem Morales inquired if there were any persons
  present who wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City
  business not elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on Agenda Item Nos. 2, CSA-2, and H-2. She also
  requested fair treatment as a resident of Inglewood and wants phone calls and emails
  responses.

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, commented on Warrants and Bills, and the time set for City
  Council Meetings.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Pro Tem Morales declared the
  meeting adjourned in the honor of Michelle Demarco, sister of Bill Thompson at the hour
  of 2:22 p.m.

  Approved this 27th day of July, 2021

  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  _____________________________
  Eloy Morales, Jr., Mayor Pro Tem
